LOAD ROOT CAUSE + INTERVENTION (2026-07-27 ~03:00). User asked why a handful of sessions produced load 256. Answer: not organic session load. A cc-context-prek session's workflow agent (wf_698b9e5b-039) built a synthetic load harness at /tmp/stress to reproduce flaky TestDiscoverCancelKillsDescendants: 36 CPU spinners + 36 exec-churn workers (2x cores each) plus supervisor.sh respawning the fleet every 5s, all daemonized to PID 1. The exec churn (fresh-written script exec + rm loops) saturates macOS first-exec code validation — XprotectService 85% CPU, syspolicyd, trustd — the exact subsystem capt-hookd SecCodeCopyGuestWithAttributes peer verification depends on, so it amplified the probe failures (6215482 / d66aaa4) machine-wide. A stray `yes` pair (01:35) and hung-looking ugreps were secondary; ugreps completed on their own once CPU freed.
Actions on explicit user directive: waited for runC to finish (30/30 pass), stopped workers via the harness's own loadstop.sh, killed the yes pair, neutered cpuload.sh/execchurn.sh/loadstart.sh in place (immutable-flagged, notice inside pointing here), killed supervisor.sh (pid 29204). Result logs in /tmp/stress preserved untouched. Load 256 -> 84 and falling. Cross-session note filed in cc-context (3d8217d). Guidance for load experiments henceforth: inside an OrbStack VM/container, never host-wide on an active machine. Fix wave for 6215482+191e5724+d66aaa4 dispatched end-to-end (daemonkit v0.20.10, captain-hook v12.20.13, local install) as workflow wf_4dc05729-4af on user approval.
